originality.rationale: The inspected full original LZ78 paper (1978) and full Ziv arXiv note (2014) give dictionary parsing and general coding bounds but no cyclic order-five enumerations. The indexed 1984 Etzion–Lempel de Bruijn complexity is linear-feedback degree, not LZ78 count. The modern LZ78 substring-query study gives algorithms, not the finite joint table. published-finding corpus searches for the exact family/parameters and direct semantic aliases returned different text-index, attractor and substring statistics. A distinct previously recorded LZ76 full-history enumeration for the same cycles does not determine the LZ78 dictionary counts. The remaining possibility of an unindexed exact table is acknowledged, not denied.

value.rationale: A cyclic de Bruijn family is fixed by uniform length-five substring inventory, yet LZ78 dictionary behavior varies with ordering and cut. The six-class exact joint profile identifies 30 fully rotation-insensitive instances and the sharp range 11–14 in a natural compression invariant. This is a full classification on 2048 nontrivial objects, not an arbitrary small sample or a re-run of known linear-complexity tabulation; it supplies a reproducible benchmark and structural contrast but asserts neither code-bit optimum nor higher-order law.
